zh.title: 台灣虎航培訓機師規模創新高　黃世惠赴安捷台東基地視察
zh.summary: 台灣虎航董事長黃世惠11月3日前往安捷航空台東基地了解學員受訓與生活情況；雙方今年規劃送訓36人，創歷年合作新高。
body: 台灣虎航持續擴大飛行員在地培育，2026年與安捷航空合作的培訓機師規模創下歷年新高。董事長黃世惠於11月3日前往安捷航空設於台東機場（TTT）的飛航訓練中心，了解學員訓練進度與學習評量，也與培訓機師交流受訓心得和職涯規劃。
根據安捷航空說明，這批學員自今年初陸續到台東基地報到，接受系統化課程、實際飛行操作及階段性評量。黃世惠此次訪視除聽取訓練進度與考核簡報，也實地了解學員宿舍、餐食和生活環境，並關心受訓期間的學習與生活需求。
台灣虎航與安捷航空於2026年3月18日第四度簽署培訓機師訓練合約，規劃全年送訓36人，為雙方歷來最大代訓規模。台灣虎航當時表示，訓練經費由公司全額負擔，並運用安捷航空的標準化課程與教官資源，協助學員建立基礎飛行技能與專業素養。
安捷航空附設飛航訓練中心成立於2014年，主要訓練基地位於台東，與台灣虎航自2015年起合作。安捷航空在今年3月公布，當時共有51名畢業校友任職台灣虎航；此數字反映截至該次公告的情況，並非此次訪視的即時人數。雙方透過合作，讓航空公司能持續掌握培訓進度並與訓練機構溝通教學需求。
安捷航空指出，飛行員養成除了專業飛行技術與嚴謹考核，也需要穩定的學習環境與生活支持。此次訪視涵蓋住宿、餐飲和訓練成果，顯示雙方將生活照顧納入人才培育安排，希望學員能在完善的環境中專心訓練。
隨著台灣虎航推動機隊汰舊換新及航網發展，穩定培育飛行員成為人力布局的重要一環。培訓學員仍須依規定完成相關訓練與考核，才能銜接後續航空公司機型訓練及航線飛行任務，這次合作則持續為國內航空產業提供在地人才培育管道。

en.title: Tigerair Taiwan chairman visits Apex Aviation training base amid record cadet intake
en.summary: Tigerair Taiwan chairman Huang Shih-hui visited Apex Aviation's Taitung training centre on November 3; their 2026 training plan covers a record 36 cadets.
body: Tigerair Taiwan is expanding its domestic pilot training programme, with the 2026 cadet intake through Apex Aviation reaching a record scale for the partnership. On November 3, chairman Huang Shih-hui visited Apex Aviation's flight training centre at Taitung Airport (TTT) to review student progress and performance assessments and to discuss training experiences and future career plans with the cadets.

According to Apex Aviation's account of the visit, cadets began reporting to the Taitung base in stages earlier this year. Their programme includes structured courses, practical flying and staged assessments. Huang received briefings on training progress and evaluations, inspected student accommodation and meal arrangements, and met the cadets to learn about their daily lives during training.

Tigerair Taiwan and Apex Aviation signed their fourth pilot training agreement on March 18, 2026. They planned to train 36 cadets over the year, making it the largest annual intake in the history of their cooperation. Tigerair Taiwan said that it would cover training expenses in full and use the academy's standardized courses and instructor resources to develop essential flying skills and professional standards.

Apex Aviation's affiliated flight training centre was established in 2014, with its principal training base in Taitung. The operator has worked with Tigerair Taiwan since 2015. In March, Apex reported that 51 graduates were then employed by Tigerair Taiwan. That was a historical figure at the time of the March announcement and should not be interpreted as an up-to-date headcount from the November visit.

Apex Aviation emphasized that developing professional pilots requires not only technical instruction and rigorous assessments but also a stable environment and support for everyday living. The chairman's inspection of accommodation, catering and training results illustrates how both companies have incorporated student welfare into their partnership to help cadets concentrate on their studies.

As Tigerair Taiwan pursues fleet renewal and network planning, pilot training forms part of its long-term workforce development. Cadets must still complete applicable training and evaluations before progressing to airline-specific aircraft qualification and line operations. The cooperation provides a domestic pathway for nurturing future professional pilots.
